description: A general counsel must approve the final state telehealth-service license application for a planned expansion and set the operational restrictions and compliance commitments that will accompany the filing, with input from healthcare regulatory, corporate, insurance, and business counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company plans to file a state application next month to expand its telehealth services.
shared_context.S2: Jordan Lee gives final approval to the application and its accompanying operating conditions.
shared_context.S3: The current draft describes the applicant as providing telehealth services through its existing corporate structure.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's routine pre-filing review, Jordan asks healthcare regulatory, corporate, insurance, and business representatives to identify any required changes before approving the package.

PF1.text: Maya confirmed during a pre-application call with the state licensing board that this filing must identify exactly two supervising physicians, even though the draft currently leaves the supervision arrangement open; the board's clarification has not yet been added to the application checklist.

PF2.text: Thomas's review of the state's professional-entity statute confirmed that the applicant must be a professional corporation rather than the company's existing LLC; he found the issue in a corporate-structure memorandum prepared for this expansion but has not circulated the conclusion.

PF3.text: Elena obtained written confirmation from the malpractice carrier that coverage for the expanded service requires a $2,000,000 per-claim malpractice limit and a cyber-liability endorsement before operations begin; those conditions are not in the current filing package.

PF4.text: Samir confirmed with the business unit this week that the approved launch is limited to pediatric behavioral-health telehealth services, not general telehealth care; the business plan still uses the broader phrase 'telehealth services.'

acceptance_conditions: The application must identify a professional corporation as the applicant.
The application must identify exactly two supervising physicians.
The approved service scope must be limited to pediatric behavioral-health telehealth services.
The operating conditions must require $2,000,000 of malpractice coverage per claim.
The operating conditions must require a cyber-liability endorsement before operations begin.
The application package must include a commitment to update the supervision information before filing.

content_checks.C3: decisions.get('service_scope') in ['pediatric behavioral-health telehealth services', 'pediatric behavioral health telehealth services', 'pediatric_behavioral_health_telehealth']
content_checks.C6: any('supervising physicians' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft leaves supervision open, while PF1 changes the application to an exact count of two supervising physicians and requires a supervision-information update commitment.
The existing LLC appears usable from the shared corporate description, but PF2 changes the applicant entity to a professional corporation and supplies the fact that must be cited for that choice.
The draft contains no insurance operating conditions, while PF3 changes them to a $2,000,000 per-claim malpractice limit and a required cyber-liability endorsement.
The broad phrase 'telehealth services' would permit a general launch, while PF4 changes the approved service scope to pediatric behavioral-health telehealth services only.
